  This is used to impersonate a service account when getting access token.

#### GatewayConfigExtProc

**Appears in:**
- [GatewayConfigSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-gatewayconfigspec)

GatewayConfigExtProc holds configuration for the external processor.

##### Fields

- **kubernetes** ([KubernetesContainerSpec](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/api/extension_types/#kubernetescontainerspec)): Kubernetes defines the configuration for running the external processor as a Kubernetes container.

- **metadataForwardingNamespaces** (string array): MetadataForwardingNamespaces lists the untyped dynamic metadata namespaces Envoy forwards
  to the external processor for this Gateway's AI traffic. A BackendSecurityPolicy using
  credentialOverride.fromDynamicMetadata receives metadata only from a namespace listed here.
  Under Envoy Gateway's mergeGateways, every Gateway in the class shares one Envoy, so a
  namespace any one of them declares is forwarded for all of their AI traffic.

#### GatewayConfigForwardProxy

**Appears in:**
- [GatewayConfigSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-gatewayconfigspec)

GatewayConfigForwardProxy configures an HTTP CONNECT forward proxy for upstream egress.

##### Fields

- **address** (string, required): Address is the `host:port` of the HTTP CONNECT proxy. The host may be a hostname or an
  IP address; the port is required. Upstream connections are tunnelled through this proxy
  via Envoy's http_11_proxy transport socket, preserving the upstream TLS session.

#### GatewayConfigSpec

**Appears in:**
- [GatewayConfig](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-gatewayconfig)

GatewayConfigSpec defines the configuration for the AI Gateway.

##### Fields

- **extProc** ([GatewayConfigExtProc](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-gatewayconfigextproc)): ExtProc defines the configuration for the external processor container.

- **globalLLMRequestCosts** ([LLMRequestCost](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-llmrequestcost) array): GlobalLLMRequestCosts defines default LLM request costs that apply to all
  routes referencing this GatewayConfig. These costs can be overridden on a
  per-route basis via AIGatewayRoute.Spec.LLMRequestCosts.
  When a request matches a route, the cost calculation proceeds as follows:
   1. If the route defines LLMRequestCosts with a matching metadataKey, use that.
   2. Otherwise, fall back to the global cost with that metadataKey (if defined here).
   3. If neither exists, the cost is not calculated for that metadataKey.
  This allows you to define common cost formulas once at the gateway level
  (e.g., billing_charges = input_tokens + output_tokens) and only override
  them in specific routes when needed (e.g., premium routes with different pricing).

- **forwardProxy** ([GatewayConfigForwardProxy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-gatewayconfigforwardproxy)): ForwardProxy routes all upstream AI/LLM traffic from Gateways referencing this
  GatewayConfig through an HTTP CONNECT forward proxy. This is intended for data planes
  in locked-down networks where direct egress to providers is not permitted and all
  outbound traffic must traverse a proxy.

GatewayConfigStatus defines the observed state of GatewayConfig.

##### Fields

- **conditions** ([Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.29/#condition-v1-meta) array): Conditions describe the current conditions of the GatewayConfig.

#### HTTPBodyField

**Appears in:**
- [HTTPBodyMutation](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-httpbodymutation)

HTTPBodyField represents a JSON field name and value for body mutation

##### Fields

- **path** (string, required): Path is the top-level field name to set in the request body.
  Examples: `service_tier`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`

- **value** (string, required): Value is the JSON value to set at the specified field. This can be any valid JSON value:
  string, number, boolean, object, array, or null.
  The value will be parsed as JSON and inserted at the specified field.
  Examples:
    - `\`scale\`` (string)
    - `42` (number)
    - `true` (boolean)
    - `\{\`key\`: \`value\`\}` (object)
    - `[1, 2, 3]` (array)
    - `null` (null)

#### HTTPBodyMutation

**Appears in:**
- [AIGatewayRouteRuleBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aigatewayrouterulebackendref)
- [AIServiceBackendSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aiservicebackendspec)

HTTPBodyMutation defines the mutation of HTTP request body JSON fields that will be applied to the request

##### Fields

- **set** ([HTTPBodyField](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-httpbodyfield) array): Set overwrites/adds the request body with the given JSON field (name, value)
  before sending to the backend. Only top-level fields are currently supported.
  Input:
    \{
      `model`: `gpt-4`,
      `service_tier`: `default`
    \}
  Config:
    set:
    - path: `service_tier`
      value: `scale`
  Output:
    \{
      `model`: `gpt-4`,
      `service_tier`: `scale`
    \}

- **remove** (string array): Remove the given JSON field(s) from the HTTP request body before sending to the backend.
  The value of Remove is a list of top-level field names to remove.
  Input:
    \{
      `model`: `gpt-4`,
      `service_tier`: `default`,
      `internal_flag`: true
    \}
  Config:
    remove: [`service_tier`, `internal_flag`]
  Output:
    \{
      `model`: `gpt-4`
    \}

#### HTTPHeaderMutation

**Appears in:**
- [AIGatewayRouteRuleBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aigatewayrouterulebackendref)
- [AIServiceBackendSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aiservicebackendspec)

HTTPHeaderMutation defines the mutation of HTTP headers that will be applied to the request

##### Fields

- **set** ([HTTPHeader](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/spec/?h=httproutetimeouts#httpheader) array): Set overwrites/adds the request with the given header (name, value)
  before the action.
  Input:
    GET /foo HTTP/1.1
    my-header: foo
  Config:
    set:
    - name: `my-header`
      value: `bar`
  Output:
    GET /foo HTTP/1.1
    my-header: bar

- **remove** (string array): Remove the given header(s) from the HTTP request before the action. The
  value of Remove is a list of HTTP header names. Note that the header
  names are case-insensitive (see
  https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2616#section-4.2).
  Input:
    GET /foo HTTP/1.1
    my-header1: foo
    my-header2: bar
    my-header3: baz
  Config:
    remove: [`my-header1`, `my-header3`]
  Output:
    GET /foo HTTP/1.1
    my-header2: bar

#### HTTPHeaderValueFilter

**Appears in:**
- [AIServiceBackendSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aiservicebackendspec)

HTTPHeaderValueFilter filters individual values out of a multi-valued request header before the
request is forwarded to this backend.

This drops (or restricts to) specific values from a comma-separated header while forwarding the
rest untouched, so one unsupported value does not fail the whole request.

Only comma-delimited headers are supported. Values are matched exactly, after surrounding
whitespace is trimmed. To remove a header entirely, use HeaderMutation.Remove instead.

##### Fields

- **name** ([HTTPHeaderName](#sigs-k8s-io-gateway-api-apis-v1-httpheadername), required): Name is the name of the header whose values are filtered. Header names are
  case-insensitive (see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc2616#section-4.2).

- **mode** ([HTTPHeaderValueFilterMode](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-httpheadervaluefiltermode)): Mode selects the filtering semantics. Defaults to Denylist.

- **values** (string array): Values is the list of header values to drop (Denylist) or keep (Allowlist).
  An empty list leaves the header unchanged.

#### HTTPHeaderValueFilterMode

**Underlying type:** string

**Appears in:**
- [HTTPHeaderValueFilter](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-httpheadervaluefilter)

HTTPHeaderValueFilterMode specifies the filtering semantics of an HTTPHeaderValueFilter.

##### Possible Values

- **Denylist** (enum): HTTPHeaderValueFilterModeDenylist drops the values listed in Values, keeping everything else.
  New values the gateway has not been configured for pass through untouched.
  

- **Allowlist** (enum): HTTPHeaderValueFilterModeAllowlist keeps only the values listed in Values, dropping everything
  else. New values the gateway has not been configured for are dropped.
  

#### JWKS

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteOAuth](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteoauth)

JWKS defines how to obtain JSON Web Key Sets (JWKS) either from a remote HTTP/HTTPS endpoint or from a local source.

##### Fields

- **remoteJWKS** ([RemoteJWKS](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/api/extension_types/#remotejwks)): RemoteJWKS defines how to fetch and cache JSON Web Key Sets (JWKS) from a remote
  HTTP/HTTPS endpoint.

- **localJWKS** ([LocalJWKS](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/api/extension_types/#localjwks)): LocalJWKS defines how to get the JSON Web Key Sets (JWKS) from a local source.

#### JWTSource

**Appears in:**
- [MCPAuthorizationSource](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpauthorizationsource)

JWTSource defines the MCP authorization source for JWT tokens.
At least one of scopes or claims must be provided.
Scopes and claims are AND-ed: when both are specified, both sets must match.

##### Fields

- **scopes** (JWTScope array): Scopes defines the list of JWT scopes required for the rule.
  If multiple scopes are specified, all scopes must be present in the JWT for the rule to match.

- **claims** (JWTClaim array): Claims defines the list of JWT claims required for the rule. Each claim must exist on the token
  and have at least one of the expected values. Use to enforce tenant or subject-based access.

#### LLMRequestCost

**Appears in:**
- [AIGatewayRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aigatewayroutespec)
- [GatewayConfigSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-gatewayconfigspec)

LLMRequestCost configures each request cost.

##### Fields

- **metadataKey** (string, required): MetadataKey is the key of the metadata to store this cost of the request.

- **type** ([LLMRequestCostType](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-llmrequestcosttype), required): Type specifies the type of the request cost. The default is `OutputToken`,
  and it uses `output token` as the cost. The other types are `InputToken`, `TotalToken`,
  `CachedInputToken`, `CacheCreationInputToken`, `ReasoningToken`, and `CEL`.

- **cel** (string): CEL is the CEL expression to calculate the cost of the request.
  The CEL expression must return a signed or unsigned integer. If the
  return value is negative, it will be error.
  The expression can use the following variables:
  	* model: the model name extracted from the request content. Type: string.
  	* backend: the backend name in the form of `name.namespace`. Type: string.
  	* input_tokens: the number of input tokens. Type: unsigned integer.
  	* cached_input_tokens: the number of cached read input tokens. Type: unsigned integer.
  	* cache_creation_input_tokens: the number of cache creation input tokens. Type: unsigned integer.
  	* output_tokens: the number of output tokens. Type: unsigned integer.
  	* total_tokens: the total number of tokens. Type: unsigned integer.
  	* reasoning_tokens: the number of reasoning tokens. Type: unsigned integer.
  For example, the following expressions are valid:
  	* `model == 'llama' ?  input_tokens + output_token * 0.5 : total_tokens`
  	* `backend == 'foo.default' ?  input_tokens + output_tokens : total_tokens`
  	* `backend == 'bar.default' ?  (input_tokens - cached_input_tokens) + cached_input_tokens * 0.1 + cache_creation_input_tokens * 1.25 + output_tokens : total_tokens`
  	* `input_tokens + output_tokens + total_tokens`
  	* `input_tokens * output_tokens`

#### LLMRequestCostType

**Underlying type:** string

**Appears in:**
- [LLMRequestCost](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-llmrequestcost)

LLMRequestCostType specifies the type of the LLMRequestCost.

##### Possible Values

- **InputToken** (enum): LLMRequestCostTypeInputToken is the cost type of the input token.
  

- **CachedInputToken** (enum): LLMRequestCostTypeCachedInputToken is the cost type of the cached input token.
  

- **CacheCreationInputToken** (enum): LLMRequestCostTypeCacheCreationInputToken is the cost type of the cached input token.
  

- **OutputToken** (enum): LLMRequestCostTypeOutputToken is the cost type of the output token.
  

- **TotalToken** (enum): LLMRequestCostTypeTotalToken is the cost type of the total token.
  

- **ReasoningToken** (enum): LLMRequestCostTypeReasoningToken is the cost type of the reasoning token.
  

- **CEL** (enum): LLMRequestCostTypeCEL is for calculating the cost using the CEL expression.
  

#### MCPAuthorizationSource

**Appears in:**

MCPAuthorizationSource defines the source of an authorization rule.

##### Fields

MCPAuthorizationTarget defines the target of an authorization rule.

#### MCPBackendAPIKey

**Appears in:**
- [MCPBackendSecurityPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendsecuritypolicy)

MCPBackendAPIKey defines the configuration for the API Key Authentication to a backend.
When both `header` and `queryParam` are unspecified, the API key will be injected into the "Authorization" header by default.

##### Fields

- **secretRef** ([SecretObjectReference](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/references/spec/#gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1.SecretObjectReference)): secretRef is the Kubernetes secret which contains the API keys.
  The key of the secret should be `apiKey`.

- **inline** (string): Inline contains the API key as an inline string.

- **header** (string): Header is the HTTP header to inject the API key into. If not specified,
  defaults to `Authorization`.
  When the header is `Authorization`, the injected header value will be
  prefixed with `Bearer `.
  Either one of Header or QueryParam can be specified to inject the API key.

- **queryParam** (string): QueryParam is the HTTP query parameter to inject the API key into.
  For example, if QueryParam is set to `api_key`, and the API key is `mysecretkey`, the request URL will be modified to include
  `?api_key=mysecretkey`.
  Either one of Header or QueryParam can be specified to inject the API key.
  Note: Embedding credentials in URLs (including query parameters) is generally not recommended because URLs can be exposed in logs
  and intermediary systems; prefer header-based injection when possible.

- **injectionPolicy** ([MCPBackendAPIKeyInjectionPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendapikeyinjectionpolicy)): InjectionPolicy controls when the configured API key is written onto the target header.
  Always (the default) writes the credential, replacing any existing value, including
  values populated by forwardHeaders.
  IfNotPresent writes the API key only if the target header is absent, so a
  caller-supplied token forwarded onto the same header is preserved.
  InjectionPolicy applies only to header injection. It must not be set to IfNotPresent
  when queryParam is used, because query-parameter injection always rewrites the backend URL.

#### MCPBackendAPIKeyInjectionPolicy

**Underlying type:** string

**Appears in:**
- [MCPBackendAPIKey](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendapikey)

MCPBackendAPIKeyInjectionPolicy controls when the configured API key is written onto the request.

##### Possible Values

- **Always** (enum): MCPBackendAPIKeyInjectionAlways writes the configured key onto the target header,
  replacing any existing value. This is the default and preserves existing behavior.
  

- **IfNotPresent** (enum): MCPBackendAPIKeyInjectionIfNotPresent writes the configured key only when the target
  header is absent, so a value already set (for example by forwardHeaders) is preserved.
  

#### MCPBackendSecurityPolicy

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendref)

MCPBackendSecurityPolicy defines the security policy for a backend MCP server.

##### Fields

- **apiKey** ([MCPBackendAPIKey](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendapikey)): APIKey is a mechanism to access a backend. The API key will be injected into the request headers.

#### MCPBackendSelector

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutespec)

MCPBackendSelector defines which of a MCPRoute's backends a request may fan out to.

##### Fields

- **defaultAction** ([AuthorizationAction](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-authorizationaction)): DefaultAction is the action to take when no rules match. If unspecified, defaults to Deny.

- **rules** ([MCPBackendSelectorRule](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendselectorrule) array): Rules defines a list of backend selection rules.
  These rules are evaluated in order, the first matching rule will be applied,
  and the rest will be skipped.
  If no rules are defined, DefaultAction is applied to every candidate backend
  (defaults to Deny).

#### MCPBackendSelectorRule

**Appears in:**
- [MCPBackendSelector](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendselector)

MCPBackendSelectorRule defines a single backend selection rule.

##### Fields

- **cel** (string): CEL specifies a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression, evaluated once for
  each backend already listed in backendRefs. It does not parse a list of backends
  out of the request. Each evaluation binds request.mcp.backend to the name of the
  one candidate backend under test, so the expression should answer `is this backend
  allowed`, not `which backends should be used`. The expression must return a
  boolean; evaluation errors or non-boolean results are treated as `no match`. A
  match means the rule applies, and Action below decides whether that's an Allow or
  a Deny for that backend.
  Example CEL expressions:
  	* `request.mcp.backend in request.auth.jwt.claims.mcp_backends`
  	* `(`,` + request.headers[`x-ai-eg-mcp-backend-subset`] + `,`).contains(`,` + request.mcp.backend + `,`)`
  Available attributes are the same as documented on MCPRouteAuthorizationRule.CEL,
  except request.mcp.method, request.mcp.tool, and request.mcp.params are not
  populated (no MCP method has been selected yet at backend-selection time).
  Note: The CEL expression support is experimental, and the attributes
  available to the expression may change in future releases.

- **action** ([AuthorizationAction](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-authorizationaction)): Action is the decision for matching backends. If unspecified, defaults to Allow.

#### MCPHeaderForward

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendref)

MCPHeaderForward specifies a header to extract from the incoming request and forward to a backend.

##### Fields

- **name** (string, required): Name is the header name to extract from the incoming client request.

- **backendHeader** (string): BackendHeader is the header name to use when forwarding to the backend.
  If not specified, the original header name is used.

#### MCPPromptFilter

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendref)

MCPPromptFilter filters prompts using include and exclude patterns with exact matches or regular expressions.
Exclude rules take precedence over include rules (deny-wins). When both include and exclude are specified,
a prompt must match an include rule AND not match any exclude rule to be allowed.

##### Fields

- **include** (string array): Include is a list of prompt names to include. Only the specified prompts will be available.

- **includeRegex** (string array): IncludeRegex is a list of RE2-compatible regular expressions that, when matched, include the prompt.
  Only prompts matching these patterns will be available.

- **exclude** (string array): Exclude is a list of prompt names to exclude. The specified prompts will not be available.
  Exclude rules take precedence over include rules.

- **excludeRegex** (string array): ExcludeRegex is a list of RE2-compatible regular expressions that, when matched, exclude the prompt.
  Prompts matching these patterns will not be available. Exclude rules take precedence over include rules.

#### MCPRouteAuthorization

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteSecurityPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutesecuritypolicy)

MCPRouteAuthorization defines the authorization configuration for a MCPRoute.

##### Fields

- **defaultAction** ([AuthorizationAction](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-authorizationaction)): DefaultAction is the action to take when no rules match. If unspecified, defaults to Deny.

- **rules** ([MCPRouteAuthorizationRule](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteauthorizationrule) array): Rules defines a list of authorization rules.
  These rules are evaluated in order, the first matching rule will be applied,
  and the rest will be skipped.
  If no rules are defined, the default action will be applied to all requests.

#### MCPRouteAuthorizationRule

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteAuthorization](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteauthorization)

MCPRouteAuthorizationRule defines an authorization rule for MCPRoute based on the MCP authorization spec.
Reference: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/draft/basic/authorization#scope-challenge-handling

##### Fields

- **source** ([MCPAuthorizationSource](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpauthorizationsource), required): Source defines the authorization source for this rule.
  If not specified, the rule will match all sources.

- **target** ([MCPAuthorizationTarget](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpauthorizationtarget), required): Target defines the authorization target for this rule.
  If not specified, the rule will match all targets.

- **cel** (string): CEL specifies a Common Expression Language (CEL) expression evaluated for this rule.
  The expression must return a boolean; evaluation errors or non-boolean results
  are treated as `no match`.
  Example CEL expressions:
  	* `request.method == `POST``
  	* `request.headers[`x-custom-header`] == `AllowedValue``
  	* `request.mcp.tool in [`toolA`, `toolB`]`
  Available attributes in the CEL expression:
  	* request.method: HTTP method such as GET or POST. Type: string.
  	* request.headers: map of headers with lowercased keys, first value only. Type: map[string]string.
  	* request.headers_all: map of headers with lowercased keys, all values. Type: map[string][]string.
  	* request.path: request path such as /mcp. Type: string.
  	* request.auth.jwt.claims: JWT claims when a bearer JWT is present. Type: map[string]any.
  	* request.auth.jwt.scopes: JWT scopes when a bearer JWT is present. Type: []string.
  	* request.mcp.method: MCP method such as tools/list or tools/call. Type: string.
  	* request.mcp.backend: upstream backend name (for example, `kiwi` or `github`). Type: string.
  	* request.mcp.tool: tool name without backend prefix (for example, `list_issues`). Type: string.
  	* request.mcp.params: parameters of the MCP method, including keys like `_meta` and `arguments`. Type: object.
  Note: The CEL expression support is experimental, and the attributes
  available to the expression may change in future releases.

- **action** ([AuthorizationAction](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-authorizationaction)): Action is the authorization decision for matching requests. If unspecified, defaults to Allow.

#### MCPRouteBackendRef

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutespec)

MCPRouteBackendRef wraps a EG's BackendObjectReference to reference an MCP server.

##### Fields

- **group** ([Group](#sigs-k8s-io-gateway-api-apis-v1-group)): Group is the group of the referent. For example, `gateway.networking.k8s.io`.
  When unspecified or empty string, core API group is inferred.

- **kind** ([Kind](#sigs-k8s-io-gateway-api-apis-v1-kind)): Kind is the Kubernetes resource kind of the referent. For example
  `Service`.
  Defaults to `Service` when not specified.
  ExternalName services can refer to CNAME DNS records that may live
  outside of the cluster and as such are difficult to reason about in
  terms of conformance. They also may not be safe to forward to (see
  CVE-2021-25740 for more information). Implementations SHOULD NOT
  support ExternalName Services.
  Support: Core (Services with a type other than ExternalName)
  Support: Implementation-specific (Services with type ExternalName)

- **name** ([ObjectName](#sigs-k8s-io-gateway-api-apis-v1-objectname), required): Name is the name of the referent.

- **namespace** ([Namespace](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/spec/?h=httproutetimeouts#namespace)): Namespace is the namespace of the backend. When unspecified, the local
  namespace is inferred.
  Note that when a namespace different than the local namespace is specified,
  a ReferenceGrant object is required in the referent namespace to allow that
  namespace's owner to accept the reference. See the ReferenceGrant
  documentation for details.
  Support: Core

- **port** ([PortNumber](#sigs-k8s-io-gateway-api-apis-v1-portnumber)): Port specifies the destination port number to use for this resource.
  Port is required when the referent is a Kubernetes Service. In this
  case, the port number is the service port number, not the target port.
  For other resources, destination port might be derived from the referent
  resource or this field.

- **path** (string): Path is the HTTP endpoint path of the backend MCP server.
  If not specified, the default is `/mcp`.

- **toolSelector** ([MCPToolFilter](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcptoolfilter)): ToolSelector filters the tools exposed by this MCP server.
  Supports exact matches and RE2-compatible regular expressions for both include and exclude patterns.
  If not specified, all tools from the MCP server are exposed.

- **promptSelector** ([MCPPromptFilter](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcppromptfilter)): PromptSelector filters the prompts exposed by this MCP server, analogous to ToolSelector.
  If not specified, all prompts from the MCP server are exposed.
  This is also used to determine which prompt names can be safely exposed unprefixed when
  this backend's effective PrefixMode is Never: only prompts named in Include are validated
  for cross-backend uniqueness and exposed bare. If unset while PrefixMode is Never, this
  backend's prompts are not exposed bare (they keep the `<backendName>__` prefix) because
  their names cannot be proven unique at admission time.

- **securityPolicy** ([MCPBackendSecurityPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendsecuritypolicy)): SecurityPolicy is the security policy to apply to this MCP server.

- **forwardHeaders** ([MCPHeaderForward](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpheaderforward) array): ForwardHeaders specifies HTTP headers to extract from the incoming client request
  and forward to this backend MCP server.
  This enables per-user authentication passthrough (e.g., personal access tokens)
  without requiring OAuth configuration.
  Each entry specifies a header name to extract and an optional rename for the backend.

- **prefixMode** ([MCPRoutePrefixMode](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteprefixmode)): PrefixMode controls how tool and prompt names from this backend are prefixed.
  Takes precedence over the route-level PrefixMode when set.

#### MCPRouteBackendTrafficPolicy

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutespec)

MCPRouteBackendTrafficPolicy configures how the Envoy Gateway BackendTrafficPolicy
resources auto-generated for a MCPRoute interact with other BackendTrafficPolicy
resources (e.g. an operator-defined rate limiting policy) targeting the same HTTPRoute.

##### Fields

- **mergeType** ([MergeType](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-mergetype)): MergeType determines how the auto-generated BackendTrafficPolicy (for example, the
  OAuth protected resource metadata policy) is merged with other BackendTrafficPolicy
  configurations targeting the same route or a parent Gateway/Listener.
  When set, the auto-generated BackendTrafficPolicy will merge with the closest parent
  BackendTrafficPolicy in the route's attachment hierarchy instead of overriding it
  entirely, per Envoy Gateway's merge semantics.
  If unset, no merging occurs, and the auto-generated BackendTrafficPolicy fully
  overrides any other BackendTrafficPolicy targeting the same route.
  See: https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/tasks/traffic/backend-traffic-policy/

#### MCPRouteOAuth

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteSecurityPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutesecuritypolicy)

MCPRouteOAuth defines a MCP spec compatible OAuth authentication configuration for a MCPRoute.
Reference: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization

##### Fields

- **issuer** (string, required): Issuer is the authorization server's issuer identity.

- **audiences** (string array): Audiences is a list of JWT audiences allowed access.
  It is recommended to set this field for token audience validation, as it is a security best practice to prevent token misuse.
  Reference: https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization#token-audience-binding-and-validation

- **jwks** ([JWKS](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-jwks)): JWKS defines how a JSON Web Key Sets (JWKS) can be obtained to verify the access tokens presented by the clients.
  If not specified, the JWKS URI will be discovered from the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata
  as per RFC 8414 by querying the `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` endpoint on the Issuer.

- **authorizationServerMetadataUrl** (string): AuthorizationServerMetadataURL is the URL the controller fetches the OAuth 2.0 Authorization
  Server Metadata document from, as defined in RFC 8414. When set, it replaces the well-known
  URIs derived from Issuer.
  Set this when the metadata lives somewhere the issuer does not lead to, for example an issuer
  of `https://example.com/api/idp/authn` whose document is served only at
  `https://example.com/api/idp/v4/authn/.well-known/openid-configuration`.
  Issuer is unaffected by this field. It continues to identify the authorization server in the
  protected resource metadata the gateway publishes, and to derive the well-known URIs when this
  field is unset. When JWKS is not set, the JWKS URI is discovered from the document fetched here.

- **protectedResourceMetadata** ([ProtectedResourceMetadata](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-protectedresourcemetadata), required): ProtectedResourceMetadata defines the OAuth 2.0 Resource Server Metadata as per RFC 8414.
  This is used to expose the metadata endpoint for mcp clients to discover the authorization servers,
  supported scopes, and JWKS URI.

- **claimToHeaders** (ClaimToHeader array): ClaimToHeaders specifies JWT claims to extract and forward as HTTP headers to backend MCP servers.
  This enables backends to access user identity for authorization, auditing, or personalization.
  Security considerations:
  - Any client-provided headers matching the configured header names will be stripped to prevent forgery
  - Only the specified claims are extracted; the full JWT is not forwarded to backends
  - Consider using a header prefix (e.g., `X-Jwt-Claim-`) to avoid conflicts with other headers

#### MCPRoutePrefixMode

**Underlying type:** string

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendref)
- [MCPRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutespec)

MCPRoutePrefixMode controls how tool and prompt names are prefixed when exposed to clients.

PrefixMode can be set at the route level (MCPRouteSpec) and overridden per backend
(MCPRouteBackendRef); the per-backend value takes precedence when set. A single route can
therefore mix Always and Never backends. This is intentional: it lets an operator keep the
route-level default (Always is recommended for most routes, since it guarantees a collision-free
catalog without any extra configuration) while opting specific, well-known backends into bare
names, e.g. to match tool names an existing client or interactive MCP App already hardcodes.
Per-backend override is meant as a targeted escape hatch, not a replacement for choosing one
naming policy for the route as a whole.

##### Possible Values

- **Always** (enum): MCPRoutePrefixModeAlways prefixes tool/prompt names with `<backendName>__`.
  This is the default and preserves existing behavior.
  

- **Never** (enum): MCPRoutePrefixModeNever exposes tool/prompt names unprefixed.
  Tool names must be unique across all Never-mode backends on the route.
  

#### MCPRouteSecurityPolicy

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutespec)

MCPRouteSecurityPolicy defines the security policy for a MCPRoute.

##### Fields

- **oauth** ([MCPRouteOAuth](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteoauth)): OAuth defines the configuration for the MCP spec compatible OAuth authentication.

- **apiKeyAuth** ([APIKeyAuth](https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/api/extension_types/#apikeyauth)): APIKeyAuth defines the configuration for the API Key Authentication.

- **extAuth** ([ExtAuth](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-extauth)): ExtAuth defines the configuration for External Authorization.

- **authorization** ([MCPRouteAuthorization](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteauthorization)): Authorization defines the configuration for the MCP spec compatible authorization.

- **mergeType** ([MergeType](#github-com-envoyproxy-gateway-api-v1alpha1-mergetype)): MergeType determines how the auto-generated SecurityPolicy for this MCPRoute (which
  enforces OAuth/JWT, API key, or external authorization) is merged with other
  SecurityPolicy configurations targeting the same route or a parent Gateway/Listener.
  When set, the auto-generated SecurityPolicy will merge with the closest parent
  SecurityPolicy in the route's attachment hierarchy (for example, one targeting a
  Gateway, Gateway listener, ListenerSet, or ListenerSet listener) instead of
  overriding it entirely, per Envoy Gateway's merge semantics.
  If unset, no merging occurs, and the auto-generated SecurityPolicy fully overrides
  any other SecurityPolicy targeting the same route.
  See: https://gateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/tasks/security/apikey-authn/

#### MCPRouteSpec

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRoute](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproute)

MCPRouteSpec details the MCPRoute configuration.

##### Fields

- **parentRefs** ([ParentReference](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/spec/?h=httproutetimeouts#parentreference) array, required): ParentRefs are the names of the Gateway resources this MCPRoute is being attached to.
  Cross namespace references are not supported. In other words, the Gateway resources must be in the
  same namespace as the MCPRoute. Currently, each reference's Kind must be Gateway.

- **path** (string): Path is the HTTP endpoint path that serves MCP requests over the Streamable HTTP transport.
  If not specified, the default is `/mcp`.

- **headers** ([HTTPHeaderMatch](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/spec/?h=httproutetimeouts#httpheadermatch) array): Headers are HTTP headers that must match for this route to be selected.
  Multiple match values are ANDed together, meaning, a request must match all the specified headers to select the route.

- **hostnames** (Hostname array): Hostnames is a list of hostnames matched against the HTTP Host header to select this MCPRoute.
  This is equivalent to the Hostnames field in the Gateway API HTTPRouteSpec. When specified, the
  generated HTTPRoute includes these hostnames, so the MCP route lands in the per-host virtual host
  instead of the wildcard vhost (the same scoping AIGatewayRoute.Hostnames provides).
  See https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/api-types/httproute/#hostnames
  for the details of the Hostnames field in the Gateway API.

- **backendRefs** ([MCPRouteBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendref) array, required): BackendRefs is a list of backend references to the MCP servers.
  These MCP servers will be aggregated and exposed as a single MCP endpoint to the clients.
  From the client's perspective, they only need to configure a single MCP server URL, e.g. `https://api.example.com/mcp`,
  and the Envoy AI Gateway will route the requests to the appropriate MCP server based on the requests.
  All names must be unique within this list to avoid potential tools, resources, etc. name collisions.
  Also, cross-namespace references are not supported. In other words, the backend MCP servers must be in the
  same namespace as the MCPRoute.

- **securityPolicy** ([MCPRouteSecurityPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutesecuritypolicy)): SecurityPolicy defines the security policy for this MCPRoute.

- **backendTrafficPolicy** ([MCPRouteBackendTrafficPolicy](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendtrafficpolicy)): BackendTrafficPolicy configures the auto-generated Envoy Gateway BackendTrafficPolicy
  resources for this MCPRoute, for example the OAuth protected resource metadata policy
  created when SecurityPolicy.OAuth is configured.

- **backendSelector** ([MCPBackendSelector](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpbackendselector)): BackendSelector restricts which of this route's backends a given request may fan
  out to, evaluated once per candidate backend when a client session is initialized.
  If unspecified, all backends on the route are considered.
  Security note: a backendSelector rule whose CEL expression reads request.auth.jwt
  (claims or scopes) only reflects verified JWT data when SecurityPolicy.OAuth is
  configured for this route; the XValidation below enforces that pairing so that
  unauthenticated or forged bearer tokens can't influence backend selection.

- **prefixMode** ([MCPRoutePrefixMode](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteprefixmode)): PrefixMode controls how tool and prompt names from all backends on this route are prefixed.

#### MCPRouteStatus

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRoute](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproute)

MCPRouteStatus contains the conditions by the reconciliation result.

##### Fields

- **conditions** ([Condition](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.29/#condition-v1-meta) array, required): Conditions is the list of conditions by the reconciliation result.
  Currently, at most one condition is set.
  Known .status.conditions.type are: `Accepted`, `NotAccepted`.

#### MCPToolFilter

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteBackendRef](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcproutebackendref)

MCPToolFilter filters tools using include and exclude patterns with exact matches or regular expressions.
Exclude rules take precedence over include rules (deny-wins). When both include and exclude are specified,
a tool must match an include rule AND not match any exclude rule to be allowed.

##### Fields

- **include** (string array): Include is a list of tool names to include. Only the specified tools will be available.

- **includeRegex** (string array): IncludeRegex is a list of RE2-compatible regular expressions that, when matched, include the tool.
  Only tools matching these patterns will be available.

- **exclude** (string array): Exclude is a list of tool names to exclude. The specified tools will not be available.
  Exclude rules take precedence over include rules.

- **excludeRegex** (string array): ExcludeRegex is a list of RE2-compatible regular expressions that, when matched, exclude the tool.
  Tools matching these patterns will not be available. Exclude rules take precedence over include rules.

#### ProtectedResourceMetadata

**Appears in:**
- [MCPRouteOAuth](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcprouteoauth)

ProtectedResourceMetadata represents the Protected Resource Metadata	of the MCP server as per RFC 9728.

References:
* https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization#authorization-server-location
* https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728#name-protected-resource-metadata

##### Fields

- **resource** (string, required): Resource is the identifier of the protected resource.
  This should match the MCPRoute's URL. For example, if the MCPRoute's URL is
  `https://api.example.com/mcp`, the Resource should be `https://api.example.com/mcp`.

- **resourceName** (string): ResourceName is a human-readable name for the protected resource.

- **scopesSupported** (string array): ScopesSupported defines the minimal set of scopes required for the basic functionality of the MCPRoute.
  It should avoid broad or overly permissive scopes to prevent clients from requesting tokens with excessive privileges.
  If an operation requires additional scopes that are not present in the access token, the client will receive a
  403 Forbidden response that includes the required scopes in the `scope` field of the `WWW-Authenticate` header.
  This enables incremental privilege elevation through targeted `WWW-Authenticate: scope=`...`` challenges when
  privileged operations are first attempted.

- **resourceSigningAlgValuesSupported** (string array): ResourceSigningAlgValuesSupported is a list of JWS signing algorithms supported by the resource server.
  These algorithms are used in the `alg` field of the JOSE header in signed tokens.

- **resourceDocumentation** (string): ResourceDocumentation is a URL that provides human-readable documentation for the resource.

- **resourcePolicyUri** (string): ResourcePolicyURI is a URL that points to the resource server's policy document.

#### ToolCall

**Appears in:**
- [MCPAuthorizationTarget](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-mcpauthorizationtarget)

ToolCall represents a tool call in the MCP authorization target.

##### Fields

- **backend** (string, required): Backend is the name of the backend this tool belongs to.

- **tool** (string, required): Tool is the name of the tool.

#### VersionedAPISchema

**Appears in:**
- [AIServiceBackendSpec](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-aiservicebackendspec)

VersionedAPISchema defines the API schema of either AIGatewayRoute (the input) or AIServiceBackend (the output).

This allows the ai-gateway to understand the input and perform the necessary transformation
depending on the API schema pair (input, output).

Note that this is vendor specific, and the stability of the API schema is not guaranteed by
the ai-gateway, but by the vendor via proper versioning.

##### Fields

- **name** ([APISchema](#github-com-envoyproxy-ai-gateway-api-v1beta1-apischema), required): Name is the name of the API schema of the AIGatewayRoute or AIServiceBackend.

- **version** (string): Version is the version of the API schema.
  When the name is set to AzureOpenAI, this version maps to `API Version` in the
  Azure OpenAI API documentation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/reference#rest-api-versioning).
  This field is ignored for OpenAI, AWSBedrock, GCPVertexAI, and Anthropic.
  For OpenAI and Anthropic, use prefix to configure custom request paths.
  See https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/capabilities/llm-integrations/supported-providers for details.

- **prefix** (string): Prefix is the prefix for the API.
  When the name is set to `OpenAI`, `chat completions` API endpoint will be `$\{this_field\}/chat/completions`.
  When the name is set to `Anthropic`, the `messages` API endpoint will be `$\{this_field\}/messages`.
  It can be with or without a leading slash (`/`).
  This field is ignored for AWSAnthropic and GCPAnthropic.
  This is especially useful when routing to a backend that has an OpenAI or Anthropic compatible API but has a different
  prefix. For example, Gemini OpenAI compatible API (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai) uses
  `/v1beta/openai` prefix. Another example is that Cohere AI (https://docs.cohere.com/v2/docs/compatibility-api)
  uses `/compatibility/v1` prefix. On the other hand, DeepSeek (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/) doesn't
  use prefix, so you can leave this field unset.
  See https://aigateway.envoyproxy.io/docs/capabilities/llm-integrations/supported-providers for details.

# A token budget for every agent: Agent Router with Agent Substrate

Source: https://theagentrouter.ai/blog/agent-substrate-token-budgets
Date: 2026-11-16

![A token budget for every agent: Agent Router with Agent Substrate](https://theagentrouter.ai/img/og/blog/agent-substrate-token-budgets.png)

[Agent Substrate](https://github.com/agent-substrate/substrate) gives every agent a verified
identity. Agent Router counts the tokens every model call spends. Connect the two and each agent
gets its own token budget from a single rate limit rule, with no custom services and no provider
key in the sandbox.

We built this as a
[runnable example](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/tree/main/examples/agent-substrate).
It sets up Substrate, Envoy Gateway and Agent Router on a kind cluster, runs against a mock model
so you don't need an API key, and comes with a test script. It's an example, not a new feature, and
we'd like to know whether it solves a problem you have. There are some questions for you at the end.

## What a per-agent budget needs

When agents share a provider key, any spending limit on that key is shared too. One agent stuck in
a loop can use up the budget for all the others, and the provider's usage report can't tell you
which agent it was.

Substrate runs agents as _actors_, each in its own gVisor or microVM sandbox, and sends their
outbound traffic through an egress gateway. That gateway decides what each actor may reach, and can
add credentials to approved requests so they never enter the sandbox. It can also mint a short-lived
JWT that names the actor. What Substrate doesn't know is what a model call cost, because that number
is in the model's response.

Agent Router reads that response, so it knows what each call cost. It only needs to be told who
made the call, and the JWT does that.

Together, they cover the three things a per-agent budget needs:

| Piece       | The question it answers       | Where it comes from here                                                                     |
| ----------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bucket key  | Which agent is this?          | The subject of a JWT signed by Substrate, verified at the gateway                            |
| Counter     | How many tokens has it spent? | Envoy Gateway's rate limit service and Redis, charged with the token count from Agent Router |
| Bucket size | How many tokens may it spend? | The `limit` on the rate limit rule                                                           |

## How it fits together

```mermaid
%%{init: {"flowchart": {"wrappingWidth": 340}}}%%
flowchart TD
    A["<b>Actor</b><br/>sandbox, no credentials"] -->|"Bearer placeholder"| B["<b>Substrate egress gateway</b><br/>checks the egress policy<br/>swaps in an actor JWT"]
    B -->|"Bearer actor JWT"| C["<b>Agent Router</b><br/>verifies the JWT<br/>keeps one bucket per actor<br/>injects the provider key<br/>counts tokens"]
    C -->|"Bearer provider key"| D["<b>Model provider</b>"]
```

The arrows show the `Authorization` header at each hop. Substrate answers _who is calling_ and
_whether it may reach Agent Router at all_. Agent Router answers _how many tokens it may spend_, and
holds the provider key.

## The configuration

Agent Router runs on Envoy Gateway, so most of this is standard Envoy Gateway policy. These are the
four parts that matter. The [docs page](https://theagentrouter.ai/docs/next/capabilities/traffic/agent-substrate) walks
through the full setup.

**Put a JWT on the actor's requests.** This Substrate egress policy lets an actor reach Agent
Router, and replaces the `Authorization` header it sends with a 15-minute JWT:

```yaml
rules:
  - http:
      hostnames: ["agent-router.envoy-gateway-system.svc.cluster.local"]
      effects:
        replaceHeaders:
          - header: Authorization
            prefix: "Bearer "
            actorJwt:
              audiences: ["agent-router"]
              expirationSeconds: 900
```

The token's subject names the actor, such as `actor/agents/actor-a`. It carries identity only, with
no budget in it.

**Verify the JWT and copy out the identity.** A `SecurityPolicy` checks the token against Substrate's
published keys and copies the subject into a header. We named it `x-actor-id`. If the agent sends
its own `x-actor-id`, this replaces it.

```yaml
jwt:
  providers:
    - name: agent-substrate
      issuer: https://idp.ate-system.svc
      audiences: [agent-router]
      remoteJWKS:
        uri: https://idp.ate-system.svc/openid/v1/jwks
        backendRefs:
          - group: gateway.envoyproxy.io
            kind: Backend
            name: substrate-idp
            port: 443
      claimToHeaders:
        - header: x-actor-id
          claim: sub
```

**One rate limit rule for every actor.** This `BackendTrafficPolicy` rule is the core of the
example. The 500 is deliberately small so the demo runs out quickly.

```yaml
rateLimit:
  type: Global
  global:
    rules:
      - clientSelectors:
          - headers:
              - name: x-actor-id
                type: Distinct # a bucket per actor
        shared: true # one bucket across every route on the Gateway
        limit:
          requests: 500 # tokens per actor per day
          unit: Day
        cost:
          request: { from: Number, number: 0 } # check on the way in, don't spend
          response: # charge the reported tokens at the end
            from: Metadata
            metadata:
              namespace: io.envoy.ai_gateway
              key: llm_total_token
```

`Distinct` creates a bucket for each value of the header, so there's no list of actors to maintain:
a new actor needs no change on the Agent Router side. Without `shared: true`, each route rule has
its own bucket, and a budget per actor quietly becomes a budget per actor per model. The token count
comes from [`llmRequestCosts`](https://theagentrouter.ai/docs/capabilities/traffic/usage-based-ratelimiting) on the
`AIGatewayRoute`.

**Keep the JWT away from the provider.** Envoy Gateway forwards the verified JWT upstream, so remove
it on the `AIServiceBackend`:

```yaml
headerMutation:
  remove:
    - authorization
```

Agent Router sets the provider key after this removal, so this is safe on every backend. We found
this one by testing. OpenAI-style backends overwrite `Authorization` with the key anyway, but a
backend that authenticates with `x-api-key` (`AnthropicAPIKey`) received the actor's JWT until we
added these lines.

With the parts not shown here (trust for Substrate's signing keys and a fixed Service name), that's
five Kubernetes resources and one Substrate policy per actor, about 130 lines of YAML on top of a
basic Agent Router install. You do need Envoy Gateway's global rate limiting turned on, which uses
Redis.

## What we tested

`test.sh` makes its calls from inside the sandboxes, through the real path. The mock model reports
200 tokens per response, and each actor has 500 tokens per day. Here's part of a run, with some
fields trimmed. `remaining` is the value before the call is charged.

```text
[PASS] 1. Actor A and actor B each complete a call; tokens are metered per actor
       rate limit counters: actor-a=200 actor-b=200
       credential the model received: actor-a=provider-key actor-b=provider-key
[PASS] 2. Actor A sends x-actor-id: actor/agents/actor-b and is still charged as actor A
       upstream saw x-actor-id: actor/agents/actor-a
       actor-a counter 200 -> 400; actor-b counter 200 -> 200
[PASS] 3. Actor A's 4th call gets 429 (500 tokens/day, 200 per call); actor B still gets 200
       actor-a call 3: {"status":200,"total_tokens":200,"remaining":"100"}
       actor-a call 4: {"status":429,"total_tokens":null,"remaining":"0"}
       actor-b:        {"status":200,"total_tokens":200,"remaining":"300"}
```

Actor A spends its budget and gets `429` on its fourth call, while actor B, with its own bucket, keeps
working. Here's the full list of what the script checks:

| When a caller...                                                         | What happens                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Makes a normal call                                                      | Its tokens are counted against its own bucket, and the model receives Agent Router's provider key                                      |
| Spends its budget                                                        | Its next call gets `429`, and other agents keep working                                                                                |
| Sends `x-actor-id` claiming to be another agent                          | The header is replaced with the verified identity, and the call is charged to the real caller                                          |
| Has no egress rule for Agent Router                                      | The name doesn't resolve in its sandbox, dialing the Service IP gets a connection reset, and nothing reaches Agent Router              |
| Isn't an actor at all, and sends no token, a forged JWT or a bare header | `401`                                                                                                                                  |
| Streams its response                                                     | It's charged when the stream ends, even though the agent didn't ask for usage: Agent Router adds `stream_options.include_usage` itself |

## What it costs

The full path (both hops, the JWT check and the rate limit check) added about 3 ms at the median and
5 ms at p95, over 2,000 non-streamed calls. That's a kind cluster on a laptop (Docker Desktop on
Apple Silicon, 8 CPUs, 24 GiB) with a mock that answers instantly, so take it as a rough figure.
Real model calls take far longer than this.

`setup.sh` reached its first successful call in three to seven minutes across our runs, on the same
laptop with warm build caches. It builds Substrate from source, so expect longer with cold caches.
We haven't timed that.

## What to watch for

- **Budgets can overshoot.** Tokens are charged when a response ends, and a request is admitted as
  long as the bucket isn't over the limit. With one call at a time, a budget of N tokens at C tokens
  per call allows `floor(N/C) + 1` calls. In the demo, 500 tokens allows three calls of 200. Calls
  that run at the same time all see the same balance, so an agent can overshoot by every response it
  has in flight.
- **A call cut off early isn't charged.** The charge comes from the usage the model reports at the
  end of the response. If the agent drops the connection before then, for example partway through a
  stream, the budget isn't charged, though the provider may still bill for the tokens. A second rule
  that limits each actor's request count puts a bound on this.
- **The demo's hop to Agent Router is plain HTTP.** The actor JWT on it is a bearer token that's
  valid for 15 minutes, so anyone who can read that traffic can replay it. That's fine on a laptop.
  Elsewhere, encrypt the hop, for example with an `https` egress rule and an HTTPS listener on Agent
  Router. We haven't tested that yet.
- **A day is a UTC day.** Budgets reset at 00:00 UTC, not 24 hours after first use.
- **The agent has to send an `Authorization` header.** Substrate's egress gateway replaces the
  header and doesn't add one. Any value works, so "no credentials in the agent" literally means
  `Bearer placeholder`. With no header, there's no JWT, and Agent Router returns `401`.
- **The provider sees the actor's ID.** `x-actor-id` travels upstream with the request, so a real
  provider would see names like `actor/agents/actor-a`. Keep the header on the request: the rate
  limit reads it again to charge the response, so if you remove it with `headerMutation`, nothing
  gets charged.
- **Agents have to call Agent Router's URL.** Point the agent's model base URL at Agent Router, and
  don't give actors egress rules to the providers. Without a rule, a provider's name won't even
  resolve inside the sandbox.

## Different budgets for different agents

The example gives every actor the same budget. The bucket key already identifies each actor, so a
different budget size is a question of where the number comes from:

- **Per-actor rules, in gateway config.** When several rules match a request, all of them apply. So
  add a rule with an `Exact` match on the actor and its own `limit`, and exclude that actor from the
  default rule with `invert: true`. We tested this on Envoy Gateway v1.9.3 with one actor at 500
  tokens and another at 5,000, and it needed no extra service. The example's
  [README](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/tree/main/examples/agent-substrate#different-budgets-per-actor)
  has the YAML. Envoy Gateway's API key authentication can also put the client ID in a header
  (`apiKeyAuth.forwardClientIDHeader`), so the same kind of rule can key on an API key instead.
- **Per-value overrides, proposed.** An open Envoy Gateway pull request,
  [envoyproxy/gateway#9771](https://github.com/envoyproxy/gateway/pull/9771), would let a `Distinct`
  rule list per-value limits without the `invert` bookkeeping.
- **Budgets from another system.** To change budgets without touching gateway config, a rule can read
  its limit from request metadata (`limit.fromMetadata`), written by an ext_authz service that looks
  up the actor.

Our first version of this demo used that last option, with about 185 lines of Go for the lookup
service. It worked, but we took it out: the actor's identity was already the bucket key, and the
service only earned its place if budgets had to change outside gateway config. If that's your
situation, it's still a good option, but you don't need it to get started.

## Try it

You need Docker, `kubectl`, `helm`, `go`, `git`, `jq` and `curl`, and about 15 GB of free disk:

```shell
git clone https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router.git
cd agent-router/examples/agent-substrate
./setup.sh   # builds Substrate from source, so it takes a few minutes
./test.sh    # 6 checks, each printing PASS or FAIL with evidence
./cleanup.sh # deletes the kind cluster
```

We ran it with Agent Router v1.2.1 and Envoy Gateway v1.9.3, against the mock model and not a real
provider. Substrate is pre-1.0 and its APIs change, so the example pins a commit. The
[README](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/tree/main/examples/agent-substrate) lists
every version and has a step-by-step walkthrough.

## Tell us what you think

Neither project needed a code change for this, and we'd like to know whether it's worth taking
further. If you run agents on Substrate, or on anything else that gives them an identity, we'd love
to hear from you:

- Would you use this, and what's missing?
- Is the same budget for every agent enough, or do you need a different size per agent?
- Should budgets live in gateway config, or in a system you already have?

Find us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/xuxtPq43gZ), or
[open an issue](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/issues).

---

# Keep LiteLLM's API, put Envoy behind it: introducing the Agent Router Python SDK

Source: https://theagentrouter.ai/blog/python-sdk
Date: 2026-11-06

![Introducing the Agent Router Python SDK](https://theagentrouter.ai/img/og/blog/python-sdk.png)

If you build agents in Python, there's a good chance LiteLLM is somewhere in your dependency tree.
It gave the ecosystem something it badly needed: one `completion()` call for every model provider.
Google ADK and the OpenAI Agents SDK both lean on it, and so do countless internal tools.

The API isn't the problem. The problem is where all the hard work happens. With a library,
fallbacks, retries, rate limits and provider keys all live inside your Python process, on every
laptop, CI runner and container that runs your agent. Production systems have a well-understood
answer to that pattern, and it's a gateway.

Today we're introducing the
**[Agent Router Python SDK](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router-python)**. It keeps
LiteLLM's API (same functions, same arguments, same response objects, same error names) and sends
every call through Agent Router, the open-source AI gateway built on Envoy. Moving over is usually
one changed import:

```python
from theagentrouter.compat import litellm   # was: import litellm
```

## Why a gateway, not a library

The SDK's design comes down to one rule: **the SDK never calls a provider itself.** Every request
goes to an Agent Router gateway, either one the SDK runs on your machine or one your team operates.
That split buys you a few things a library can't:

- **Resilience runs in the gateway, not your process.** Fallbacks, retries and request limits are
  defined once and enforced by Envoy, the same proxy that already carries production traffic at a
  large share of the internet's infrastructure. Every program on the machine, or every service
  pointed at the shared gateway, gets the same behavior.
- **Provider keys stay on the gateway.** Point the SDK at a shared gateway with two environment
  variables, and laptops and CI jobs hold a client key, not your OpenAI, Anthropic or Bedrock
  credentials.
- **A much smaller footprint.** `theagentrouter-core` has exactly one runtime dependency: `httpx`.
  There are no provider SDKs, and the model catalog ships with each release instead of being
  downloaded on import. After this year's supply-chain incidents across the Python ecosystem,
  including the [compromised LiteLLM releases in March](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026),
  a small dependency surface and keys that never touch the client are worth more than ever.
- **One observability story.** Instead of per-library logging integrations, the gateway emits
  OpenTelemetry traces and metrics for every call.

## Your first call

```shell
pip install theagentrouter
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...
```

```python
import theagentrouter

resp = theagentrouter.completion(
    model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarise yesterday's refunds"}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

There's no server to start. On the first call, the SDK starts a local Agent Router gateway, writes
its config from the provider keys in your environment, and routes the call through it. The gateway
keeps running in the background and is shared by every program on the machine that uses the SDK.

The SDK covers the APIs agents actually use:

- `completion` / `acompletion`, with streaming, tools, structured output and thinking
- OpenAI's Responses API via `theagentrouter.responses()`
- Anthropic's Messages API via `theagentrouter.anthropic.messages.create()`, in Anthropic's native
  format, so prompt caching and thinking work as you'd expect
- `embedding`, `token_counter`, cost and model-info helpers

OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek and Together are
supported today. Claude calls go to the gateway in the Messages format; everything else in OpenAI's
format.

## Coming from LiteLLM: change one import

For your own code, swap the import and leave the rest alone. `completion` arguments,
`ModelResponse` objects, streaming chunks, `RateLimitError` and `ContextWindowExceededError`,
`success_callback`, `mock_response`, `completion_cost`, `token_counter` and even `Router` all
behave the way your code expects.

The SDK is deliberately honest about the edges, too. LiteLLM arguments that would do nothing here,
such as a per-call `fallbacks=` or `caching=`, don't silently disappear; each one warns the first
time it's used, and the docs tell you what to do instead. Functions outside the agent use case
(image generation, speech, `text_completion`) aren't included, so code that relies on them fails
loudly with `AttributeError` rather than misbehaving. The full table lives in
[Coming from LiteLLM](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router-python/blob/main/docs/coming-from-litellm.md).

If you'd rather hand the migration to your coding agent, the repo ships a
[migrate-from-litellm](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router-python/tree/main/skills/migrate-from-litellm)
skill. Drop it into your agent's skills folder (for Claude Code, `.claude/skills/`) and ask it to
migrate the project.

## Fallbacks, retries and limits, defined once

A **route** is a model name you choose, with real models behind it in order:

```python
import theagentrouter as ar

ar.route(
    "chat",
    primary="openai/gpt-5.4",
    fallbacks=["anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"],
    retry=ar.Retry(attempts=2),
    limit=ar.Limit(60, per="minute"),
)

ar.completion(model="chat", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
```

In this example, a call to `chat` goes to `gpt-5.4`. On a connection failure or a 429, 500, 502,
503 or 504, the gateway retries up to twice more, then moves to Claude. A 401 doesn't trigger a
retry. Requests beyond 60 a minute get a `RateLimitError`. Give `primary` a list and the route
spreads traffic across several models.

The gateway also deals with the cross-provider details that usually break hand-rolled fallbacks.
For example, when a request falls back from Claude to a newer OpenAI model, `max_tokens` becomes
`max_completion_tokens`, and parameters a newer Claude model refuses are stripped before the
request reaches it.

Routes are saved to `~/.agentrouter/routes.json`, so every program on the machine shares them. If
your code already uses LiteLLM's `Router` with `fallbacks` and `num_retries`, its model groups are
turned into gateway routes automatically.

## Agent frameworks, no LiteLLM required

Google ADK and the OpenAI Agents SDK both import `litellm` internally. One call makes that import
resolve to Agent Router instead, so neither framework needs LiteLLM installed:

```python
from theagentrouter.compat import install_as_litellm
install_as_litellm()  # before importing the framework

from agents import Agent, Runner
from agents.extensions.models.litellm_model import LitellmModel

agent = Agent(
    name="refunds",
    instructions="Answer questions about refunds.",
    model=LitellmModel(model="anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"),
)
print(Runner.run_sync(agent, "How much was refunded yesterday?").final_output)
```

ADK works the same way through its `LiteLlm` model class.

## From laptop to production without changing code

The local gateway is for development. For staging and production, run Agent Router as a shared
gateway and point your code at it:

```shell
export AGENTROUTER_BASE_URL=https://gateway.acme.example/v1
export AGENTROUTER_API_KEY=...
```

With these set, the local gateway never starts and calls go to the shared one. The SDK sends the
same requests to both, so code that works on your laptop works in production. In servers,
containers, serverless functions and CI, you can install just `theagentrouter-core` and skip the
local gateway entirely.

To get to a shared gateway quickly, export the setup you've been using locally:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from theagentrouter import local_gateway

Path("config.yaml").write_text(local_gateway.export_config(port=1975))
```

The exported configuration can be used to run a gateway with the
[Agent Router standalone mode](https://theagentrouter.ai/docs/cli/aigwrun). It checks one shared client key: pick any
value, set it as `AGENTROUTER_API_KEY` on the server, and give your clients the same value.

## Locked down by default, even on your laptop

A developer gateway holding real API keys should be treated like production, and the local gateway
is configured that way:

- It answers only callers on the same machine (`127.0.0.1` and `::1`), matched on the connection's
  source address, so a forged header can't get around it.
- It checks the `Host` header, so a malicious web page can't reach it through DNS rebinding.
- Its config file contains no key values. Each key is written to its own file with narrow
  permissions, and is removed when the gateway stops.

## What's not there yet

The SDK is in alpha (`0.1.0a12`), and at the time of writing these are the known limitations:

- The bundled local gateway runs on macOS 13+ on Apple Silicon and on Linux with glibc 2.36+
  (x86-64 and Arm). On Windows, Intel Macs and older Linux, the SDK installs without it and needs a
  remote gateway.
- Google Vertex AI isn't wired into the local gateway yet. Use `gemini/...` for the Gemini API.
- Image generation, speech, transcription, files and batches are not yet supported.

## Try it out

```shell
pip install theagentrouter
```

- Check out the code, docs and more than 20 runnable examples:
  [github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router-python](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router-python)
- Learn about the gateway:
  [github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router)
- Questions and feedback: the [Agent Router Discord](https://discord.gg/xuxtPq43gZ)

If you try it on a real LiteLLM codebase, we would love to hear your feedback! Open an issue, or
tell us in Discord.

---

# Agent Router 1.2: safe to share across users and teams

Source: https://theagentrouter.ai/blog/v1.2-release-announcement
Date: 2026-10-09

![Agent Router 1.2: safe to share across users and teams](https://theagentrouter.ai/img/og/blog/v1.2-release-announcement.png)

**Agent Router 1.2 is out.** It is the first release since Envoy AI Gateway became Agent Router,
and nothing you deploy is renamed: same CRDs, same Helm charts, same `aigw` CLI.

The short version: 1.2 makes the gateway safe to share. Safe to put your MCP tools in front of real
users. Safe to run one gateway for many teams. And easier to trust when something goes wrong in
production.

## Put MCP tools in front of real users

When an agent calls a tool through the gateway, the gateway decides who the caller is and what they
can touch. 1.2 tightens every step of that decision:

- **Only verified identity counts.** Authorization rules read JWT claims only from tokens Envoy has
  verified, and the token's issuer must match the one you configured.
- **Broken rules deny.** A CEL policy that errors at runtime now blocks the call instead of being
  skipped.
- **Sessions belong to one user.** An MCP session is bound to the user who started it, so someone
  else can't reuse its session ID.
- **No shared default key.** The Helm chart generates a random session encryption seed instead of
  shipping a well-known one.

## MCP that fits the clients you already have

- **Clean tool names.** Clients that hardcode tool names, such as MCP Apps, can see `search_issues`
  instead of `github__search_issues` (`prefixMode: Never`).
- **Bring your own token.** Users can forward a personal token, such as a GitHub PAT, and fall back
  to a shared service key when they don't (`injectionPolicy: IfNotPresent`).
- **Keep your Gateway-wide policies.** Gateway-level rate limits and ext-auth can now stay in force
  alongside MCP OAuth instead of being replaced (`mergeType`).
- **More identity providers.** Point the gateway at the exact OAuth metadata URL when your provider
  doesn't serve it at the standard path.

## One gateway, many teams

When several teams share a gateway, one team's config should never reach another team's
credentials. In 1.2, a BackendSecurityPolicy can use a Secret in another namespace only when that
namespace allows it with a ReferenceGrant, for every credential type. A grant that names an object
now covers only that object, and revoking a grant takes effect right away.

## Fewer surprises in production

- **Rotated credentials apply immediately.** This fixes a 1.1.0 regression where upstream calls
  could fail with a stale key until the next reconcile.
- **Compare providers side by side.** GenAI metrics now carry the backend, so you can compare
  latency, time to first token, and token usage for the same model across providers.
- **Per-tenant token limits charge the right tenant**, and streaming usage is recorded even when the
  client disconnects right after the last chunk.
- **Clear errors.** Calling an endpoint a provider doesn't support returns 422, not 500.
- **Smoother rollouts.** The controller reports Ready only after its caches sync, and the webhook
  certificate survives `helm upgrade` and Argo CD syncs.

On the provider side, 1.2 adds Amazon Bedrock's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (no translation hop) and
TypeSafe System One. It also filters `anthropic-beta` flags per backend, so one unsupported flag no
longer fails the whole request, and counts OpenAI prompt-cache writes in your cost metrics.

## Before you upgrade

Some of these fixes change behavior. Upgrade from 1.1.x (not directly from 1.0.x), and check these
first:

1. **Upgrade Envoy Gateway to v1.9.2 and the Gateway API CRDs to v1.6.**
2. **Expect MCP clients to reconnect.** The new random seed ends active sessions. A temporary
   fallback seed keeps them alive.
3. **Match `oauth.issuer` to your identity provider's `iss` exactly**, trailing slash included.
4. **Add `securityPolicy.oauth`** to any MCPRoute whose CEL reads `auth.jwt`, and make CEL
   null-safe.
5. **Add ReferenceGrants** for credential Secrets in other namespaces.
6. **Review per-tenant token limits.** They are now enforced correctly, so tenants may start seeing
   429s.

The [v1.2 release notes](https://theagentrouter.ai/release-notes/v1.2) have the full list and step-by-step upgrade guidance.

## Get involved

1.2 came from 39 contributors, many of them contributing for the first time. The next release can
include you.

**Get involved:**

- **Come to the weekly community meeting.** We meet every Monday.
  [Join on Zoom](https://zoom-lfx.platform.linuxfoundation.org/meeting/91546415944?password=61fd5a5d-41e9-4b0c-86ea-b607c4513e37)
  and add your questions, use cases, or demos to the
  [agenda](https://docs.google.com/document/d/10e1sfsF-3G3Du5nBHGmLjXw5GVMqqCvFDqp_O65B0_w/edit?tab=t.0).
- **Join the [Agent Router Discord](https://discord.gg/xuxtPq43gZ)** to ask questions and talk to
  the maintainers.
- **Help build what's next.** Work is under way on the stateless 2026-07-28 MCP specification,
  [OAuth token exchange for MCP backends](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/issues/2036),
  a dedicated MCPBackend CRD,
  [longer quota windows](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/issues/2469), and
  [agent-to-agent (A2A) traffic](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/issues/2070).
  Share your requirements on the issues, or pick one up.
- **Tell us how you use Agent Router.**
  [Add your logo](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/edit/main/site/src/data/adopters/adopters.json)
  to the adopters page, or share your story in Discord.
- **Send your first pull request.** Start with
  [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

Thank you to everyone who wrote code, reviewed pull requests, reported bugs, and joined the
community meetings during the move to Agent Router.

**[Get started with Agent Router 1.2](https://theagentrouter.ai/docs/getting-started/)** and
[star the repository](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router).

# Envoy AI Gateway is becoming Agent Router, an Agentic AI Foundation project

Source: https://theagentrouter.ai/blog/envoy-ai-gateway-is-now-agent-router
Date: 2026-09-09

![Agent Router. Formerly Envoy AI Gateway. Joining the Agentic AI Foundation on 10 September.](https://theagentrouter.ai/img/og/blog/envoy-ai-gateway-is-now-agent-router.png)

On 10 September, **Agent Router**, previously **Envoy AI Gateway**, officially joins the
**Agentic AI Foundation**.

Same code. Same maintainers. New home.

## A new home

Envoy AI Gateway started as an Envoy sub-project within the CNCF. On 10 September it becomes a
standalone project and moves into the Agentic AI Foundation.

This is great news for the community. The AAIF is home to the agentic stack ecosystem, and being
part of it puts Agent Router closer to the projects and people building that stack. We get to
collaborate more directly, and keep building the solutions that power agents together with everyone
else in the foundation.

## What does not change

Nothing you deploy is renamed. The product name changes in prose only.

- **CRDs and API group stay as they are.** `AIGatewayRoute`, `AIServiceBackend`,
  `BackendSecurityPolicy`, and the `aigateway.envoyproxy.io` API group are not being renamed.
- **The CLI is still `aigw`**, and the `envoy-ai-gateway-system` namespace stays the same.
- **Same maintainers, same release cadence, same Apache 2.0 license.**
- **Envoy stays underneath.** Agent Router is still built on Envoy and Envoy Gateway.

Your manifests from yesterday apply tomorrow. There is nothing to migrate.

## What does change

- **The name.** Envoy AI Gateway becomes Agent Router.
- **The repository** moves to
  [`theagentrouter/agent-router`](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router). Old
  `envoyproxy/ai-gateway` links redirect.
- **The website** moves to [theagentrouter.ai](https://theagentrouter.ai). Every
  `aigateway.envoyproxy.io` link redirects to the same page.
- **Community chat** moves to the [Agent Router Discord](https://discord.gg/xuxtPq43gZ).
  The weekly community meeting continues as before.

## Where to go next

- [Get started](https://theagentrouter.ai/docs/getting-started/) or try it with one command on your laptop:
  `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... aigw run`
- [Star the repository](https://github.com/theagentrouter/agent-router) and open issues and
  discussions there from now on.
- [Join the Discord](https://discord.gg/xuxtPq43gZ) and the
  [weekly community meeting](https://zoom-lfx.platform.linuxfoundation.org/meeting/91546415944?password=61fd5a5d-41e9-4b0c-86ea-b607c4513e37).

Thank you to everyone who built, adopted, reviewed, and championed Envoy AI Gateway over the
past two years. The name on the door is new. The people behind it, and the code, are the same.

**Agent Router configures. Envoy handles the traffic.**
